questions.q: What is one of the things Zoe will explicitly NOT do?
options: Answer inbound calls 24/7
Collect a payment or take a deposit / card
Recognize returning clients by phone
Detect and filter spam
questions.explain: Zoe never collects payment or takes a deposit/card; the salon takes payment its normal way.

questions.q: How does Zoe recognize a returning client?
options: By asking the caller to state their name
By a downloaded client app
By the phone number they're calling from, matched to the client list
By voice recognition of the caller
questions.explain: Returning callers are matched on the phone number they're calling from, pulled from the salon's client list and booking history.

questions.q: How does Zoe's spam shield actually work?
options: It blocks junk calls before they ring, using a caller-reputation database
It answers, then tags very short calls and obvious robocalls as spam after the call
It forwards all suspicious calls to a human
It requires callers to pass a verification challenge first
questions.explain: The spam shield is post-call tagging of very short calls and obvious robocalls, not a pre-answer wall or third-party reputation database.

questions.q: About how long does a standard booking call with Zoe typically run?
options: 60-120 seconds
10-20 seconds
4-5 minutes
15-30 minutes
questions.explain: A standard booking call runs about 60-120 seconds; a quick hours question is 30-60 seconds and a messy reschedule can take 4-5 minutes.

questions.q: What is the core differentiator of how Zoe handles bookings?
options: She texts the caller a booking link to complete later
She only works with Calendly
She writes the appointment into the salon's existing scheduler, live on the call
She emails the salon to enter the booking manually
questions.explain: Zoe writes the appointment end-to-end into the scheduler the salon already runs on, live on the call.

questions.q: Which two platforms are described as TRUE integrations through the salon's own account?
options: Booksy and Vagaro
Square and Mindbody
Fresha and GlossGenius
Zoca Scheduling and Boulevard
questions.explain: Square and Mindbody are true integrations via the salon's own account; Booksy, Vagaro, Fresha, and GlossGenius use the secure-assistant approach.

questions.q: Why does Zoe book without collecting a deposit or card on the call?
options: Because the schedulers don't support deposits
It's a deliberate feature so most bookings land confirmed instead of stuck awaiting payment
Because deposits are illegal over the phone
Because she can't access the salon's deposit settings
questions.explain: Deposits-off is deliberate; with no payment step to stall on, most Zoe bookings land confirmed and the salon's deposit settings stay untouched.

questions.q: What is the correct, customer-safe way to describe how Zoe connects to Booksy, Vagaro, Fresha, and GlossGenius?
options: An official API partnership
A reverse-engineered workaround
A secure automated assistant set up on the account using the salon's login
A manual data export each morning
questions.explain: The honest framing is a secure automated assistant on the account using the login; never say official API partnership, hacky, or workaround.

questions.q: Who provides and pays for Zoe's dedicated phone number?
options: The salon, as a monthly add-on
Zoca provides and pays for it, and the owner can pick the area code
The salon's existing carrier
Google, via the Business Profile
questions.explain: Zoca provisions and pays for a US/Canada number, and the owner can choose the area code so it feels local.

questions.q: How does the salon keep its existing number while using Zoe?
options: By forwarding its existing line to Zoe's number
By instant self-serve porting of the number to Zoca
By replacing all signage with the new number
By using two separate phones at the front desk
questions.explain: The salon forwards its existing line to Zoe's number via a guided wizard; a true self-serve port-in is only on the roadmap.

questions.q: What does Zoe's transfer/handoff capability look like today?
options: A warm transfer to multiple destinations
A cold transfer to one destination during transfer hours
No transfer is possible at all
An automatic transfer to a call center
questions.explain: Today it's a cold transfer to one destination per salon during transfer hours; warm transfer and multiple destinations are on the roadmap.

questions.q: How long does Zoe's guided onboarding take, and how many steps does it have?
options: A multi-day IT project across 20 steps
About 5 minutes, fully self-serve, 3 steps
About 45 minutes (rarely over an hour), 10 steps
About 2 hours, 7 steps
questions.explain: Setup is a guided ~45-minute, 10-step onboarding ending with a free test call and go-live.

questions.q: Which two Training tab sections are REQUIRED to go live?
options: QnAs and Policies
Business Profile and Services
Custom Instructions and QnAs
Services and Policies
questions.explain: Business Profile and Services are the two required-to-go-live sections; QnAs, Policies, and Custom Instructions fine-tune her.

questions.q: How many voices can the owner choose from for Zoe?
options: Four (Eryn, Vexa, Mark, Jessica)
Two (male and female)
Unlimited via voice cloning
Six, one per salon type
questions.explain: The owner picks one of four voices (Eryn, Vexa, Mark, Jessica); there is no voice cloning.

questions.q: How does the 'Questions from calls' Brain loop work?
options: Zoe mines transcripts and invents memories automatically
Zoe surfaces questions she couldn't answer, and the owner's answer becomes knowledge
An AI auto-answers every gap without owner input
The owner must re-record the whole Training tab weekly
questions.explain: Zoe surfaces questions she couldn't fully answer; the owner answers, and that answer becomes permanent knowledge, keeping the owner in control.

questions.q: What is Configs, the flagship upcoming feature?
options: A live feature today for warm transfers
A way to clone the owner's voice
Rules so Zoe acts more like the owner, e.g. offering an on-the-spot discount (not live yet)
A second calendar for Zoe to manage
questions.explain: Configs (~1-2 months, flagship) will let Zoe act like the owner, headlined by on-the-spot discounting, but it isn't live and shouldn't be demoed as such.

questions.q: Which dashboard tab serves as the inbox of every call and text Zoe handled?
options: Overview
Bookings
Activity
Analytics
questions.explain: The Activity feed is the inbox; there's no separate Inbox tab, and it shows transcripts, AI summaries, and recordings.

questions.q: What does L2B (Lead-to-Booking) do?
options: It calls every abandoned lead by voice immediately
When someone abandons a web booking, Zoe texts them back and re-books in the thread
It exports leads to a spreadsheet for manual follow-up
It blocks repeat callers from booking twice
questions.explain: L2B recovers abandoned web bookings by SMS today, with booking tools inside the text thread so the customer can confirm right there.

questions.q: How should the 'revenue saved' Impact number be presented?
options: As an audited accounting figure
As a guaranteed result
As an estimate showing the scale of value, used directionally
As the salon's actual measured profit
questions.explain: The Impact figure is an estimate the system calculates to show the kind of value Zoe drives, never a guarantee or audited number.

questions.q: What can the owner NOT do with the Activity feed in v1?
options: Read a full SMS thread
Play an inline recording
Jump in and reply as themselves from the feed
See the AI summary of a call
questions.explain: The v1 feed is read-only; the owner can read threads but can't reply as themselves, and human SMS take-over is on the roadmap.

questions.q: What is the Front Desk standalone monthly price and what's the included voice minute pool?
options: $99/mo with 100 voice minutes included
$349/mo with unlimited minutes
$239.20/mo with 500 voice minutes
$49/mo with 50 voice minutes
questions.explain: Front Desk standalone is $99/mo with 100 voice minutes included; year-2 renewal is $149/mo.

questions.q: How does the free trial work?
options: 30 days free, no card required
7 days free, card on file required, first $99 auto-charges unless cancelled
14 days free, billed in advance
No trial is offered
questions.explain: There's a 7-day free trial with a card on file; the clock starts at onboarding completion and the first $99 auto-charges unless cancelled.

questions.q: Roughly what does a human receptionist cost, per the comparison that closes deals?
options: About $5/hour
About $99/month total
About $25/hour, easily a few thousand dollars a month
About $1/minute
questions.explain: A human receptionist runs roughly $25/hour, easily a few thousand a month, and still goes home, takes lunch, and handles one call at a time.

questions.q: What is 'the core win' against competitors repeated throughout the docs?
options: Zoe is the cheapest tool available
Zoe offers unlimited voice minutes
Zoe books into the salon's existing calendar end-to-end on the call, while rivals send a link or only do Calendly
Zoe ships a mobile app for clients
questions.explain: The core win is that Zoe writes the booking into the salon's existing calendar end-to-end on the call, unlike rivals that send a link or only support Calendly/Google Calendar.

questions.q: Which of these is something Zoe will NOT do?
options: Transfer to a human during forwarding hours
Impersonate a human (she discloses she's AI if asked)
Send SMS confirmations and reminders
Follow up on abandoned web bookings
questions.explain: Zoe never impersonates a human and discloses she's AI if asked; that's a deliberate trust and compliance choice.

questions.q: If a prospect is on no scheduler at all, what's the move?
options: Run Zoe in info-only, no-booking mode
Put them on Zoca Scheduling
Decline the deal entirely
Have Zoe email bookings to the salon
questions.explain: A connected platform is required with no booking-less mode, so a prospect with no scheduler should go on Zoca Scheduling.

questions.q: Which platform is on the roadmap with no connector yet, so AEs shouldn't promise it works today?
options: Square
Booksy
Boulevard
GlossGenius
questions.explain: Boulevard is on the roadmap with no connector yet; Acuity and StyleSeat are being explored, not supported.

questions.q: What is the universal carrier fallback for turning call forwarding on and off?
options: Dial *72 to turn forwarding on, *73 to turn it off
Dial #1 to forward, #0 to stop
Press 9 then the destination number
Forwarding can't be toggled manually
questions.explain: The forwarding wizard supports 28+ carriers with a universal fallback: dial *72 to turn forwarding on and *73 to turn it off.

questions.q: Which statement about Zoe's memory today is TRUE?
options: She recalls what a client got last visit
She carries preferences like 'always book me with Sarah' across calls
She recognizes returning callers by phone and sees upcoming appointments
She reads and writes client notes for allergies and VIP status
questions.explain: Today Zoe recognizes callers by phone and sees upcoming appointments; past-visit recall, cross-call preferences, and client notes are all roadmap.

questions.q: What is the correct customer-safe framing of the 'revenue saved' Impact number?
options: An audited accounting figure
An estimate showing the scale of value, used directionally not as a guarantee
A guaranteed minimum return
The salon's verified added profit
questions.explain: The Impact number is an estimate to show the scale of value, used directionally and never presented as audited or guaranteed.

questions.q: Which competitor ships no voice receptionist at all?
options: Rosie
Smith.ai
GlossGenius
Slang.ai
questions.explain: GlossGenius ships no voice receptionist; Slang.ai is restaurant-only and Smith.ai books Calendly only.

questions.q: How should an AE handle a salon that insists Zoe must enforce deposits / collect a card on the call?
options: Promise it and turn on the deposit toggle
Improvise a workaround on the spot
Escalate to Ashish, Robin, Chintan, Kushagra, or Piyush; don't promise it
Tell the salon it's impossible and end the call
questions.explain: The deposit-enforcement toggles are intentionally off; building it on is a product decision, so the AE should escalate to the named people, not promise or improvise.
